why: The 14:25 bridge repeats Amaziah's killing, which 14:19 has just narrated; trim it to the succession and name Jeroboam II so 'He restored' has a subject

bridges.2 Kings 14:25: Amaziah's son Azariah takes Judah's throne. In Israel, Jehoash's son Jeroboam II reigns forty-one years and does evil, yet wins back Israel's lost land.

why: Judah's king is Azariah at 15:1 but 'Uzziah' from 15:13 on (and in 2 Chronicles 26) with no hint they are the same man

bridges.2 Kings 15:5: Azariah, also called Uzziah, reigns fifty-two years and does right, though the high places remain.

why: 12:16 jumps back from David's coronation at Hebron to his outlaw days in 'the hold' with no signal, so 'betray me to mine enemies' is baffling

bridges.1 Chronicles 12:16: Earlier, while David was still hiding from Saul, warriors from many tribes had come over to him.

why: 17:4 'Go and tell David my servant' has no speaker or addressee; restore 17:3 (God's word comes to Nathan that night) and drop one line of the long psalm

David chooses the LORD's hand at 21:13, and at 21:15 the angel is suddenly destroying Jerusalem; the plague itself (seventy thousand dead) is missing. Drop the stray one-verse Ahithophel list entry instead
12:9 'So Shishak king of Egypt came up' follows from nothing: Shishak is never introduced and the prophet's rebuke and Rehoboam's repentance are skipped

bridges.2 Chronicles 12:9: In Rehoboam's fifth year Shishak king of Egypt invades. When the prophet Shemaiah rebukes them, the king and princes humble themselves, so God spares Jerusalem from destruction.

why: 17:1 'Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his stead' comes right after Hanani's rebuke; Asa's death is never mentioned

bridges.2 Chronicles 17:1: Asa dies after a severe disease in his feet, during which he sought physicians rather than the LORD.

why: 23:13 'And she looked' has no antecedent (Athaliah is last named in 22:11 and the bridge doesn't mention her); restore 23:12 and drop a lone list verse about the treasurers
34:14 'when they brought out the money that was brought into the house' refers to a temple repair the reader never saw

bridges.2 Chronicles 34:14: In his eighteenth year Josiah sends men to repair the temple with the money the Levites have collected.

why: 13:4 'And before this' points at nothing, and Tobiah's being an Ammonite is what makes his lodging in the temple an offense

bridges.Nehemiah 13:4: Reading the law, the people find that no Ammonite or Moabite may enter God's congregation, and they separate themselves from all foreigners.
